title: Can I turn our product-demo recordings into short support videos?
summary: Reuse product-demo recordings to answer recurring support questions, with complete task context, current interface footage, and clear source-based edits.
body_markdown:
## What you’ll take away


- Organize videos by the user's question rather than the original call agenda.
- Include the starting state and visible result of the task.
- Retire or update answers when the product workflow changes.


## Choose a question users actually repeat


Start with a specific support request, such as where to change a setting or how to hand a file to another person. A broad product tour is not the same as an answer. The video should let someone recognize their problem from the title and reach the relevant explanation quickly.


In an illustrative demo archive, several calls explain how to submit a review request. The useful support video shows the required starting state, the action, and what confirms completion. It does not need the sales introduction or the rest of the product tour.


## Find the clearest complete explanation


In Wideframe, identify the approved demo sources and ask for passages answering the exact question. Use the[soundbite recipe](https://try.wideframe.com/skills/find-soundbites/) to add the recurring search task when needed. Consider clarity and current product behavior, not merely the shortest answer.


Watch the screen as well as listening to the words. A speaker may explain the task correctly while the recorded cursor or interface shows something else. Choose the source that gives the learner a coherent view, or pair the explanation with a clean current capture.


## Remove the call context that a new viewer lacks


References to “your account,” “the thing we discussed earlier,” or a customer's particular setup may confuse a general support audience. Choose boundaries that avoid those dependencies or add concise editorial context. Do not publish private call details as incidental background.


If the useful answer is inseparable from a customer-specific situation, record a clean explanation using a suitable demonstration workspace. Existing footage is a resource, not an obligation to reuse every sentence. A short pickup can produce a better support asset than extensive patching.


## Show the full task, including the result


Begin with the necessary prerequisite: which screen the user is on, what they need access to, or what must already exist. Show the key action and the resulting state. Ending immediately after a click can leave the viewer unsure whether it worked.


Keep important error or exception information when it applies to ordinary users. If an explanation assumes a particular account capability, state that scope. Do not remove it merely to make the task look universal.


## Make the answer easy to follow silently too


Use readable captions and concise on-screen labels where helpful. Keep text away from the control or result the viewer needs to see. If a dense screen is unreadable in the destination, create a clearer crop or capture instead of relying on verbal instructions alone.


Wideframe's[caption workflow](https://try.wideframe.com/skills/captions/) can prepare the text delivery. Review product terms and control names carefully, then finish the actual source-based sequence in Premiere. The useful output is a short lesson someone can act on, not a transcript pasted over a busy recording.


For a repeatable caption pass, add and save[caption-this](https://try.wideframe.com/skills/caption-this/) from its setup prompt in a blank Wideframe chat. Invoke it on the finished support sequence and choose a captions track, SRT, or burned-in delivery. The recipe separates cue readability from visual titles, so keep interface labels and numbered instructions as their own editorial decisions rather than squeezing them into the spoken captions.


## Publish one current answer per question


Give the asset a clear task title and a current owner. Keep the source project and product context available for future edits. If the process changes, update the existing answer or clearly retire it rather than leaving several contradictory versions in circulation.


Use the support team's feedback to refine the explanation. If viewers repeatedly ask the same follow-up, the video may omit a prerequisite or end too early. Add the missing information instead of simply producing more clips from the archive.


## Turn new demos into future answers


After later demos, note especially clear explanations of recurring tasks. Save their source locations under the relevant support question. This makes the archive easier to reuse without treating every recorded sales call as a public tutorial.


Return to the assistant when a new question appears or a product update affects an old answer. The repeated job is finding the right explanation and preparing a current, standalone edit.


## Try this request


TRY AN EXAMPLE REQUEST


Find the clearest complete explanation of \[support question\] in these approved demo recordings. Include the starting state, action, and result. Flag customer-specific references or outdated interface details, and prepare a short source-based answer for editing.
